function.arguments: {"research_topic":"Reconstruct the Internet Research Agency's 2016 United States social-media influence operation using only evidence returned by the benchmark tools. Gather and cite the exact source IDs provided by the tools, prioritizing primary sources: relevant United States Department of Justice indictments and court filings; United States Senate Select Committee on Intelligence findings; platform-provided data or disclosures from Facebook, Twitter, Google, Reddit, and other platforms where available; and official investigative or congressional records. Build an evidence map covering: factual allegations and their procedural status; identified or alleged organizations, funders, employees, contractors, personas, pages, groups, channels, websites, and accounts; funding flows and organizational relationships; operational activities such as content creation, impersonation, advertising, account management, targeting, amplification, and election-related actions; stated or inferred campaign objectives; and relationships among entities and events. For every item, distinguish verified facts from allegations, platform-reported facts, analytical assessments, and uncertainty. Record exact names and identifiers only when present in returned sources; do not invent entities, IDs, relationship names, or links. Identify contradictions, discrepancies, scope limitations, and unresolved inconsistencies across sources, including differences in counts, dates, attribution, account ownership, reach, funding, and objectives. Return a structured research dossier suitable for a final Markdown report plus one fenced JSON object with arrays named findings, claims, reasoning_steps, and contradictions. Each finding must have question, answer, supporting_entities, and source_references; each claim must have claim and source_references; each reasoning step must have id, conclusion, premise_entities, and premise_relations; each contradiction must have contradiction_id, description, and source_references."}
function.name: ConductResearch
